| **Ahrefs** | 2025-06-26 | **81,947 sites** | AI up about 9.7x YoY, now **0.25%** of total traffic; ChatGPT over 80% of AI referrals; **Google still 210x** |
| Similarweb | 2026-09-03 | clickstream, Jun 2025 to May 2026 | **770.7M AI referral visits/month worldwide, +117.4% YoY** |
| Similarweb | 2026-07-29 | same | Gen-AI platforms 9.5B monthly visits (+70%), 655M unique visitors (+57%). Share of gen-AI visits: ChatGPT about 76% to about 53%; Gemini under 9% to about 27 to 28%; Claude about 2% to about 9% |
| Semrush / Datos | 2026-04-07 | over 1B lines US clickstream, Oct 2024 to Feb 2026 | ChatGPT outbound referrals +206% in 2025, plateaued near 1B monthly visits from Nov 2025; **web search enabled on only 34.5% of queries, down from 46%**; Google takes 21.6% of ChatGPT's outbound clicks |
| SparkToro | 2026-06-09 | Similarweb panel, US, Jan to Apr 2026 | **68.01% of Google searches end without a click** (vs 60.45% in 2024). **Only 0.34% of searches reached AI Mode** |
| Previsible | 2026-07-06 | 166 GA4 properties, 6.77M LLM sessions | ChatGPT 92.4% of trackable standalone-LLM referrals; 644,478 monthly LLM sessions May 2026, 9.9x Nov 2024; **Perplexity -61% from its Mar 2025 peak**; Copilot -96% from peak |
| **Pew (non-vendor)** | 2025-07-22 | 68,879 searches, 900 US adults, Mar 2025 | With an AI summary, users clicked a traditional result on **8%** of visits vs **15%** without. Clicks on links **inside** the summary: **1%** |

CTR studies, for the record and their weaknesses: Ahrefs 2025-04-17 (300,000 keywords, aggregated GSC, position one, desktop) found 0.026 actual vs 0.040 forecast, **-34.5%**, updated 2026-02-04 to **-58%**; the control group is "informational keywords without AIO", which Google itself selects, and the counterfactual is a straight-line forecast over a convenience panel. **Seer Interactive** (Tracy McDonald, 2025-11-04, 3,119 search terms, 42 client organizations, 25.1M organic impressions) found Q3 2025 organic CTR year over year at 0.52% when an AIO was present and not cited (-65.2%), 0.70% when present and cited (-49.4%), and **1.45% with no AIO at all (-46.2%)**. **The finding everyone drops is that non-AIO queries also fell 46.2%**, so a large share of the decline is not attributable to AI Overviews. Semrush (10M+ keywords, Jan to Nov 2025) reports AIO trigger rates of 6.49% in January, a 24.61% July peak and **15.69% in November, a pullback that is underreported**, and finds that holding keywords constant, zero-click **fell** from 33.75% to 31.53%.

First-party disclosures are useless. Alphabet's Q2 2026 CEO letter (2026-07-22) says "We're now sending billions of clicks to websites every week through AI features in Search" with no denominator, no baseline, no definition and no year-over-year. OpenAI (2026-02-27) discloses "more than 900M weekly active users" and **nothing about search-query volume, citation rates, outbound clicks or referral traffic.** Anthropic and Perplexity disclose nothing. The conversion claim people quote is **n=1**: Ahrefs' Patrick Stox, 2025-06-16, reported 0.5% of visitors driving 12.1% of signups **on ahrefs.com's own site over 30 days**, with his own caveats that AI-search users click links 75% less and the novelty may erode. It has been laundered into "AI search visitors convert 23x higher" as a general fact. The post is honest; the citations of it are **(c)**.

## 3.10 Therefore: what the skill scores, shows, and ignores

| Signal | Treatment | Why |
|---|---|---|
| robots.txt permits OAI-SearchBot, GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-User, Claude-SearchBot, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended, with no blanket `*` disallow catching them | **Score, high weight** | (a)+(b): OpenAI documents that blocking OAI-SearchBot removes you from ChatGPT search; Grossman measured 21 Google-Extended blockers with zero Gemini citations; Botify shows retrieval crawl now exceeds training crawl |
| Main content, title, headings, prices and internal links present in the **raw** HTML with no JS | **Score, high weight. The highest-value AI check there is** | (b): Vercel 2024-12-17 plus searchVIU 2025-10-30 plus Brave's source-traced fetcher |
| No stray `noindex`, `nosnippet`, `max-snippet:0`, `data-nosnippet`, `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` | **Score, high weight** | (a): Google's own doc names these as the AI-surface controls. A one-line check almost nobody runs |
| Dates: ISO 8601 with timezone, not future, **matching a visible on-page date to the day**, sitemap `lastmod` agreeing | **Score** | (a) verbatim, plus Illyes' binary-trust rule. Note the limit: a stale page with a bumped date passes every mechanical test; detecting it needs two crawls |
| JSON-LD parses, `@context` is `https://schema.org`, `@type` resolves, **every human-readable string value appears in the rendered visible text** | **Score as rich-result correctness** | (a): the visible-text rule is the one Google documents in exact words |
| "Has schema" | **Detect, never score as AI visibility** | Ahrefs matched DiD: AIO -4.6%, nulls elsewhere. Google documents no effect |
| Canonical resolves in one hop, low 404 rate, no duplicate URL patterns | **Score** | (a)+(b): Brave rejects any redirect; ChatGPT wastes 34.82% of fetches on 404s |
| Section length and heading hygiene | **Show as hygiene, no effect size** | Flag sub-50-word orphan sections (SE Ranking's honest baseline) and unbroken multi-hundred-word walls. Never state a 120 to 180-word target |
| Real `<table>`/`<ul>`/`<ol>` versus div-and-`<br>` fakes | **Show as semantic correctness only** | No citation-lift evidence exists |
| About page, contact route, byline linking to a live bio, `Organization` with resolving `sameAs` | **Score under trust-signal completeness, with the caveat printed** | (a) as rater rubric, (c) as ranking claim |
| `rel=author`, `Person` schema, editorial-policy page | **Detect, score neutral** | `rel=author` dead since 2014-08-28; no measurement exists for the others |
| `llms.txt` | **Detect, score neutral, never flag absence.** Fetch it in order to say it does not matter | Ahrefs 137,210 domains: 97% never fetched, zero probes for nonexistent files |
| Core Web Vitals | **Score under classic Search, never under AI** | Google hedges; no AI platform documents a threshold except Brave's |
| Human-readable URL slug, title semantically close to the target question | **Show, low weight** | Ahrefs 1.4M prompts: natural-language slugs 89.78% vs 81.11% opaque, title-to-prompt cosine 0.602 cited vs 0.484 non-cited. **Provenance problem: the page says "1.4 million ChatGPT 5.2 prompts from February 2025" for an April 2026 publication and discloses no source. Use cautiously** |
| A numeric spam score from HTML features | **Never emit** | Fabrication. Name the pattern, name the policy it resembles, state that intent is not determinable |

Five cross-cutting warnings worth printing in the report itself: the dominant variable is not page-side, so an HTML-only audit scores the weak half of the evidence; effect sizes get laundered by baseline removal; attribution is being fabricated in the AI-written SEO blogosphere, so a statistic with no reachable primary after two hops should be treated as invented; source mixes are not stable enough to plan against, so any citation-share percentage without a date is worthless; and the best-designed studies keep returning nulls, which a credible auditor should be willing to report.

---

# 4. Fabricated or unverifiable statistics in circulation

Do not cite any of these. Several were traced to the page they are attributed to and found absent.

| Claim | What is actually true |
|---|---|
| "Vercel analysed 500 million GPTBot fetches and found zero JS execution" | **Secondary-source fabrication.** The article states no N for the rendering test; the 569M figure is a monthly volume number retrofitted onto the rendering claim |
| "2.8x more likely" and "68.7% of ChatGPT-cited pages followed sequential heading structure from 12,000+ URLs", attributed to an AirOps page | **Verified absent from that page. The attribution was fabricated somewhere in the chain** |
| BrightEdge's "44% schema" study | **Does not exist.** The real BrightEdge 44% concerned AI Overviews criticising brands |
| "Brand mentions beat backlinks 3-to-1" | Derived by dividing two Spearman coefficients (0.664 and 0.218), which is not a valid operation |
| "AI search visitors convert 23x higher" | Laundered from Ahrefs' n=1 post about ahrefs.com's own site over 30 days |
| "Roughly half of AI-cited content is less than 13 weeks old"; "content under 30 days old earns 3.2x more citations"; "82% citation rate for content updated within 30 days falling to 37%"; "content has a 1-year half-life, each year reduces visibility 40 to 60%" | No openable primary for any of them |
| **"Perplexity weights freshness at 40% of its ranking signal, ChatGPT prioritizes referring domains at 30%, Gemini focuses on E-E-A-T at 35%"** | **Prima facie fabricated.** No lab publishes retrieval-signal weights, and Perplexity's crawler documentation does not mention freshness at all |
| "Tables boost citations 28 to 40%"; "a table is cited 34% more often than prose"; "three or more comparison tables earn 25.7% more citations"; "tables achieve an 81% extraction rate vs 23% for paragraphs"; "17.3% citation lift from structure alone across six engines" | All (c). No verifiable study compared `<table>` or `<ul>` presence in cited versus non-cited pages |
| "AI crawlers impose tight 1 to 5 second timeouts"; "TTFB under 2 seconds ensures full retrieval"; "if server response exceeds 200 ms crawlers reduce request rate" | No AI platform documents any timeout, rate limit, latency requirement or caching policy. The only documented figure anywhere is Brave's 10 s / 2 MB |
| "ChatGPT's fetcher abandons slow sites, and some sites see HTTP 499 on 5% of ChatGPT crawler visits" | An anecdote with no logs, no site list, no sample size, no date range and no timeout value |
| "AI referrals are 0.15% to 0.25% of total global internet traffic", attributed to Similarweb | **Not on either Similarweb page.** Their FAQ says only "a low single-digit percentage of most sites' total traffic" |
| "70.6% of AI traffic arrives without referrer headers" | Unverified |
| 2026 Cloudflare crawl-to-refer ratios (Anthropic 2,237:1, OpenAI 217:1, Mistral 3,389:1, Google 4.6:1) | Come only from third-party blogs reading the live Radar page, which returned HTTP 403 to every fetch attempt. The 2025 figures from Cloudflare's own posts are usable, with Cloudflare's own caveat that native-app traffic sends no `Referer` so the ratios "may overstate" |
| 2026 IndexNow adoption (5 billion daily submissions, 22% of clicked URLs, 80 million sites) | Absent from blogs.bing.com/webmaster, bing.com/indexnow, bing.com/indexnow/getstarted and the BWT IndexNow help page |
| X card specs: 1.91:1, 1200x628, 300x157 minimum, 4096x4096 maximum, 2:1 for `summary_large_image` | X publishes nothing. The 1.91:1 figure is Facebook's number borrowed. Only "less than 5MB", 420-char alt and 70-char title survive, in a **2026-02-01** Wayback snapshot |
| Slack's 2 MB image limit | Slack documents no image limits at all |
| LinkedIn's 7-day cache and the full `LinkedInBot` UA string | Folklore |
| "Unfurlers use HEAD" | Zero platforms document it |
| Named repeat-offender sources | everything-pr.com's "Citation Source Index" series (methodology is "source-weight modeling calibrated to each engine's retrieval architecture", which is a model output, not a measurement), 5WPR's PRNewswire "State of AI citations 2026", and roughly two dozen programmatically generated "statistics roundup" domains |

Performance folklore not to ship as findings: "more than N third-party scripts is bad"; "limit preconnects to 2 or 4"; "add `decoding=async` to images" (MDN says the effect is hard to perceive); "self-hosting fonts is always faster" (web.dev measured the opposite, reporting that "sites using third-party fonts had a faster render"); "images more than 2x their display size fail" (the documented rule is 4 KiB of wasted bytes against *rendered* size, which you cannot compute); "put third-party scripts at the end of body"; "convert to WebP and save X%"; woff2 size caps; and the `media="print" onload="this.media='all'"` snippet.

# 5. Could not verify

Everything here was looked for and not confirmed from a primary source. Keep the label.

**Crawler roster.** OpenAI Operator, Atlas or agent UA (absent from the bots page as fetched). Anthropic's full UA strings (the support article names tokens only). The status of legacy `anthropic-ai` and `claude-web` (absent from the current article; harmless to keep in a robots.txt but never report their absence as a finding). `Google-Firebase` and `Google-Safety` tokens (on a special-case crawlers page that was not fetched). xAI or Grok crawler documentation (none found; a Grok reply on X claiming an iPhone UA is not documentation). ByteDance official documentation (none found). Diffbot and Timpi. You.com's exact UA string (from search snippets, not a direct fetch). Bing's crawler help page content (JS-rendered, did not yield to WebFetch). Common Crawl's crawl-delay support.

**Cloudflare.** Whether `Content-Signal` exists as a general HTTP response header (it appears on Markdown for Agents responses only). Live `radar.cloudflare.com/ai-insights` values and all 2026 crawl-to-refer figures derived from them (403 on every attempt).

**Google.** The Search Console "Search generative AI" control page, reported as rolled out globally 2026-08-31 with values Include / Exclude / Inherit from parent, covering AI Overviews, AI Mode and generative AI in Discover (support.google.com/webmasters/answer/16908024, reported by one fetch, not independently re-verified, medium confidence). Whether `&num=100` was ever officially acknowledged beyond a relayed spokesperson quote. The circulating impression-drop percentages (87.7% / 77.6%). Whether `urlTestingTools.mobileFriendlyTest` still returns results.

**Bing.** Whether Bing honours `Link: <…>; rel="canonical"` in an HTTP header (no Microsoft doc either way, unlike Google; flag header-only canonicals as a risk, not an error). The `data-snippet` attribute in Webmaster Guidelines §10 (matches nothing else Microsoft published, probable editing error). Microsoft's position on llms.txt (searched blogs.bing.com, the full BWT help centre and learn.microsoft.com; nothing. **This is an absence of documentation, not a documented rejection, and must be phrased that way**). 2026 IndexNow adoption statistics.

**Emerging protocols.** The exact Lighthouse Agentic Browsing audit ids and weights. WebMCP's exact Chrome and Edge version numbers (secondary sources).

**GEO evidence.** Growth Memo's primary (paywalled, and its two secondary sample descriptions conflict). The Mueller Reddit thread `r/TechSEO/1q0mtzh` (logged-out interstitial; quotes are Search Engine Roundtable's reproduction, and SER prefaced them "this is not official guidance"). Search Engine Land's Core Web Vitals-and-AI and ChatGPT-citations articles (403). Illyes at Search Central Live APAC 2025 and his 2026-07-16 lastmod remark. Profound's 100,000-prompt overlap matrix. Conductor's "57% outside top 10". BrightEdge's Feb 2026 update and its unstated sample size. The AirOps/Indig, Digital Applied, SearchAtlas and Fischman schema studies (known only through a third-party review). Ahrefs' 1.4M-prompt study provenance. Originality.AI's AIO study (URL 404s). The "2.8x" and "68.7%" heading statistics (**verified absent from the page they are attributed to**). Every circulating freshness percentage other than Ahrefs' 16.975M-URL study. Whether any measured effect of Person schema, `sameAs` or `legalName` exists.

**Performance.** Chrome's exact unused-preload console string (the 3 s constant is verified in Blink source, the message literal is not). The literal `img { aspect-ratio: attr(width)/attr(height) }` UA stylesheet rule (**it is not in the HTML Standard**; the spec defines a presentational-hint mapping to `auto w / h`). The exhaustive per-element list of which elements' `width`/`height` map to aspect-ratio. `ispe` being mandatory for every AVIF image item (the clause is in paywalled ISO/IEC 23008-12). **The PageSpeed Insights API quota, not documented by Google anywhere fetchable.** `font-display` block and swap durations in current spec text (only a 2016 Chrome blog states 3 s / 100 ms). Whether the 4 KiB `uses-responsive-images` and 8 KiB `uses-webp-images` thresholds are still current (pages dated 2019). Whether `compression.zstd` exists in every distributor's Python 3.14 build. RFC 9842's title, date and status (seen only in the IANA registry). Current Safari behaviour for the combined `rel="preconnect dns-prefetch"` bug (2019 source). Whether any live origin emits 103 over HTTP/1.1 (zero across seven origins). The "these directives do not fall back to default-src" list as a quoted enumeration (it is the complement of the documented fallback list, so treat it as (a)-derived, not (a)-quoted). Whether an official Chrome docs page exists for the `unsized-images` audit (both paths 404).

**Security.** Consent Mode v2's EEA enforcement date, commonly cited as March 2024, not found on any fetchable Google page. Microsoft's 2025 bulk-sender requirements. Whether `<form action="http://">` is blocked or merely warned in 2026 browsers. Documented rate limits for Cloudflare or Google DoH JSON. The full error-code enumeration for the hstspreload preloadable and removable APIs. ICANN's WHOIS port-43 sunset date. The common DKIM selector list (`google`, `default`, `dkim`, `k1`, `s1`, `s2`, `mandrill`, `zoho`) against primary docs.

**Local and entity.** A standalone Google "author markup best practices" URL. schema.org release dates before 30.1. Manku et al.'s exact 64-bit fingerprint and Hamming distance k=3 near-duplicate parameters (ACM returned 403 and the WWW2007 mirror is gone; cite the paper, not the numbers). **A Google page blessing "multiple location pages that add unique value" (none was found; do not cite one).** WCAG 3.0's current status.

# 6. Not checkable from outside

These need owner attestation or a logged-in console. Say so in the report. Never score them, and never report them as missing.

| Thing | Why it is invisible | What to do instead |
|---|---|---|
| **IndexNow setup** | The key filename is the shared secret, so `/{key}.txt` cannot be discovered by probing. No `.well-known` path exists (zero "indexnow" occurrences in the IANA registry). No HTML tag, response header or sitemap element carries a signal. Blind endpoint probes returned **429** from both Bing and the generic endpoint, measured 2026-09-21. Cloudflare Crawler Hints fires from cache-MISS signals, invisible in the response | If the owner supplies a key: `GET https://{host}/{key}.txt`, assert 200, `body.strip() == key`, `Content-Type` not HTML, no auth redirect. Assert `keyLocation` prefix scoping. Report "not externally verifiable, owner attestation required" |
| **Search Console verification via DNS, and Bing verification via XML file, CNAME or Domain Connect** | Three of Bing's four methods leave no HTML trace. DNS TXT verification leaves none either | Check `msvalidate.01` and `GET /BingSiteAuth.xml` as **info**. Absence proves nothing |
| **The Search Console "Search generative AI" control** | A property-level Include / Exclude / Inherit setting rolled out globally **2026-08-31**, covering AI Overviews, AI Mode and generative AI in Discover. **A site can be absent from AI surfaces with a perfectly clean HTML profile** | Name it in the report as a thing to check in the console. Medium confidence, not independently re-verified |
| **Search Console shipping and returns settings** | Verbatim: "settings configured in Search Console will take precedence over structured data on your site" | Note the precedence when reporting shipping or return markup |
| **DKIM selectors** | No DNS enumeration mechanism exists. A guess-list miss proves nothing; eight common selectors on a plainly mail-sending domain all returned NXDOMAIN | Report **unknown**, never missing |
| **CDN dashboard bot settings** | Cloudflare's AI traffic categories (Search / Agent / Training) and "block only on pages that display ads" are account-side, and the ad-gated variant means enforcement differs page by page | Report "differential response by User-Agent observed" plus whether the zone is on Cloudflare (`cf-ray`) |
| **IP-verified allow rules** | An auditor is not on any bot's verified IP range, so a verified-bot allowlist never matches the probe. A 403 to a spoofed GPTBot UA can be a false positive | Never say "GPTBot is blocked" from a UA probe |
| **Bing Webmaster Tools AI Performance** and **Google's Search Generative AI performance reports** | Account-side citation reporting. Bing's help page is explicit: "A citation… does not represent traffic, clicks, or user engagement" | Point the owner at them; do not model them |
| **Whether `dateModified` is honest** | A stale page with a bumped date passes every mechanical test | Needs two crawls. Say so |
| **Whether a crawler renders JavaScript on this site** | Requires server logs with a JS-injected beacon | Test what is actually checkable: does the content exist in the raw response |
| **Core Web Vitals field values** | Not derivable from HTML. CrUX requires an API key, and returns 404 by design for noindexed pages | Use CrUX directly, report HTML proxies as best practice present or absent |
| **Real AI referral volume for this site** | Native-app and copy-paste traffic lands in Direct and will never be attributable | Filter referrer hosts `chatgpt.com`, `chat.openai.com`, `perplexity.ai`, `gemini.google.com`, `claude.ai`, `copilot.microsoft.com` in the owner's own analytics, and state the gap |
| **X link-preview behaviour** | No live documentation, no working validator (`cards-dev.x.com/validator` 307s to a login page) | Emit the tags, grade absence low, say the behaviour is untestable without posting |
| **Consent behaviour** | Most CMPs inject `gtag('consent','update')` at runtime | Report the **default** call (which must be synchronous and before the tag, so it is genuinely static) at high confidence, everything else as a hint |
| **Video indexing's most important requirement** | "The indexed watch page must be performing well in Search before its video can be considered for indexing" has no HTML signal at all | State it as a known blind spot |
| **Whether a spam pattern is a violation** | Every Google spam policy except the `rel` rule on paid links turns on purpose, intent or value ("primarily for the purpose of", "with the intent to", "little to no value", "human review") | Name the pattern, name the policy it resembles, state that intent is not determinable |
